div.div:
This is the re-scan form (algo::gsplat::Gsplat): one pass per destination segment, so the source is swept P times and the tier moves A(P) = P·(1 − e−w/P) bytes per live byte.
That is fine while P is small and ruinous when it is not — at a terabyte with 32 GiB it is thirty-odd sweeps. The ordering was never the problem; the re-reading was.
The staged form removes it (algo::staged::StagedSplat) by spilling into RAM-sized buckets, at a fixed 2·(stages + 1) sequential passes whatever P is. The two are level at four
segments — below that this diagram is the cheaper algorithm, because it never touches scratch. See gsplat-staged-dataflow for the other one.
